slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
Should Brightwork launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027, and how should it be packaged and priced to lift net revenue retention from 101% to 105% by 2028 with gross margin at or above 75%?
Will customers pay for Copilot, and how many?
Does Brightwork need Copilot to compete with Routewise, and what is it worth?
Which package and price earn the most?
Does Copilot meet the margin and NRR goals, and is it worth the mobile delay?
How should the launch run, and what would make us change course?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO and executive team, approving the 2027 plan
Net revenue retention reaches 105% by 2028; Company gross margin stays at or above 75%; The 14-engineer build and the two-quarter mobile delay earn their keep
January 2027 planning meeting
Building an in-house AI model; Changing the Core plan price; Hiring beyond the 60 engineers

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a per-seat Pro tier, not a $149 add-on, and plan on about $2.9M of new ARR, not $8M
Customers will pay, but expect about 14% take-up, not the survey's 46%
–	17 of 120 beta accounts paid $149 after the free period
Copilot restores parity, but win-backs are worth at most about $640K a year
–	The sales memo's claim implies a 58% win rate
A Pro tier at $12 more per seat beats the add-on and prices heavy use fairly
–	Pro adds about $2.9M of ARR, against $2.5M for the add-on
–	Add-on buyers ran nearly twice the average requests
In Pro, Copilot clears the NRR gap, holds margin and outweighs the mobile delay
–	About 5 percentage points of NRR against a gap of 4
–	The mobile delay risks at most $1.1M of ARR
Launch Pro in Q2 2027 with a seat allowance; restart the mobile rewrite in Q3
–	About 667 requests per seat a month, packs above it
